rsm:WasteTransfer.rsm:RemarkText:
Connahs Quay Power Station has no active sewer connection and instead has historically operated three separate effluent treatment plants to treat all the human sewage / waste water on site to a clean standard prior to discharge out into the River Dee with all the other cooling waters.
In the last year all three plants have suffered multiple failures due to age and failing internal mechanisms. A chain bucket lift utilised in each plant to move waste failed completely and parts are no longer available. Therefore Uniper is currently part way through a major upgrade project to moernis all three plants and replace the bucket lifts with new state of the art equipment. In the meantime Uniper are tankering off all waste sewage from the installation for treatment at local United Utilities treatment plants. So of the 2870.43 tonnes of non hazardous waste disposed from Connah’s Quay PS in 2024, 2771 tonnes were human sewage / septic tank waste. A return to outage season with two major outages completed in 2024 involving large numbers of contractors is also partially responsible for this high disposal figure .
The volumes of hazardous waste arising from the installation have grown due to increased levels of outage maintenance on the ageing power station.

rsm:PollutantRelease.rsm:RemarkText: mass emission is calculated based on extractive testing carried out throughout the year – slight discrepancies between flow rates, emission results, and run times are compounded when calculated out for the year.
the increase has been seen due to increased dosing through K8 SNCR to achieve emission limits – optimisation of the SNCR system was undertaken in 2024 and has subsequently reduced considerably

A27 (K8) – annual average calculated from quarterly monitoring increased from 0.016 in 2023 to 0.018 2024 A32 (WESP 21) – result in 2023 was 0.00092, result in 2024 0.0014, additionally with an increase in the average flow rate from 229,633 to 291,856.
A27 (K8) – annual average calculated from quarterly monitoring reduced from 0.0485 to 0.0286 A32 (WESP 21) – annual average result reduced from 0.054 to 0.023

All HCl results during quarterly compliance testing were in consent, however measured flow rates varied such that the average in 2023 was 10% less than in 2024, in addition to the increase in average flow rate from HCl monitored sources, one result in 2024 was considerably higher than any other result from that year or the previous year. At the time this was investigated and no reason could be found for the increase in the middle triplicate test. All other HCl results were below 1mg/m3, however in Q1 2024 on WESP 21 the middle 30min triplicate result was 21.1mg/m3, pushing the average for that quarter to 8.3mg/m3. We debated leaving this potentially spurious result out of the calculations for 2024 but included it in the end for completeness.

rsm:WasteTransfer.rsm:RemarkText: The increase in the reporting figure was mostly due to changes in raw material – with additional cleaning of recycled timber through the Preproduction department in 2024. Additionally, issues with the biomass boiler meant 12% more wood dust was sent off site in 2024 vs 2023.

Generation of APC residues increased in the first half of 2024, prior to the K8 shutdown where optimisation of the abatement system took place – additional hydrated lime / activated carbon was used to control emissions to atmosphere leading to an increase in APCr by 40%. Boiler ash generation from the two biomass boilers also increased by 15% - this correlates to longer running hours from the boilers for the year.

Biggest reduction was seen in the amount of waste oil / fuel removed from site. A diesel spill occurred in 2023 on the rail siding that resulted in approximately 50T being removed in 2023. The reduction in oil / water generation was also seen in general site activities.

rsm:WasteTransfer.rsm:RemarkText: Less waste reported for 2024 compared to previous years because our waste is now disposed of via a different route. Prior to 2024, most of our waste went to UK incinerators and given a D10 code (Incineration on land). The waste now goes via a process called “Energy to Waste”. The waste is sent over to mainland Europe via Forward Waste to incinerators that convert all that energy from burning into power for the grid. Because of this, they can provide an “R” code for recovery, specifically R1 (Use principally as a fuel or other means to generate energy).

rsm:PollutantRelease.rsm:RemarkText: The increase in 2024 compared to 2023 is attributed to a higher total solvent input and increased fugitive emissions. The rise is linked to greater coating line activity across our two coating lines Es3 & CR2, changes in batch campaign frequency, and increased ventilation from storage and usage points. While abatement systems operated within acceptable parameters, destruction efficiency was slightly below the target in some periods, contributing to the rise. The overall emission level remains below the PRTR reporting threshold, and further controls are being reviewed for 2025

rsm:WasteTransfer.rsm:RemarkText: Several resins currently produced are specialist resins and they have a lower tolerance to rework or process water. A change in the waste contractor used to remove UF effluent from site has resulted in a change in disposal route, reducing the amount of waste recycled off-site

• We have been continuing the programme of removing a load of legacy waste that was allowed to build up prior to 2023. • The product mix has moved to more specialist resins, that have a lower tolerance to rework of resin/process water. • We changed the waste contractor that removes UF effluent from site. This company classes this waste as disposal rather than recycled, as the old contractor did. • Change in the basis of safety for PF resin manufacture, so can no longer recycle PF washwater via this route
